lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Érica Maria Machado Santarem | Lesson 21 -- Making Comparisons
lesson.grammar_point: comparative adjectives (-er than, more ... than, better / worse)

listenings.text: Hi, Érica. It's Mark. Thank you for the coffee today. São Paulo is amazing. It's much bigger than Boston, and it's noisier too. My hotel is in Pinheiros. It's quieter than the hotel on Paulista Avenue, and it's cheaper. Tomorrow I want to go to a good restaurant. Please tell me a good place tomorrow at the office. See you at nine. Bye!

Hello, and welcome to Weekend Tips. Today, two places near São Paulo. Santos is on the beach. It is hotter than São Paulo, and the trip is short, about one hour and a half by car. Campos do Jordão is in the mountains. It is colder than São Paulo, and it is quieter. In July it is very beautiful, but it is more expensive. The hotels are cheaper in Santos. So, what is better for you? The beach, or the mountains?

items.situation: Mark asks: Is São Paulo colder than Boston? Answer him.
Compare your house and the office. Which one is quieter?

Mark wants a park. Compare Ibirapuera Park and Paulista Avenue.
Your daughter asks: São Paulo or Boston? Say one thing better and one thing worse in São Paulo.
